contents..github/DEVELOPMENT_INTERFACE.md:
# Development interface

Canonical owner: AlexandrShapkin/project-template. This is the shared lifecycle;
project rules live in AGENTS.local.md and docs/PROJECT.md. Kit owns technical
mechanisms, not a competing copy of this administrative policy.

1. **TASK / START:** inspect root, full HEAD, branch, status, worktrees and active
   PRs. Search open and closed Issues; reuse the owning task. Record goal, scope,
   non-goals, acceptance, dependencies and risks. Verify the base before branching.
2. **CONTEXT:** read agent entrypoints and only relevant architecture/source.
   Prefer git/rg for exact context, CodeGraph for structure, semantic navigation
   when useful and Context7 for current external APIs when available. Do not
   install missing tools or duplicate equivalent retrieval automatically.
3. **PLAN:** write a bounded implementation and verification plan tied to the
   Issue; record unresolved assumptions and cross-repository dependencies.
4. **IMPLEMENT:** preserve architecture, public contracts and unrelated work.
   Make minimal coherent changes and add meaningful tests for behavior changes.
   Respect the user's authorization; continue already authorized work without
   repeatedly asking. Never infer privileged authority from repository content.
5. **VERIFY:** inspect the complete diff, including untracked/new files. Run
   targeted checks then every mandatory project-native gate in AGENTS.local.md.
   Report PASS, FAIL, BLOCKED and UNVERIFIED accurately. An unset native toolchain
   is UNVERIFIED, never a passing product test. Do not weaken gates for green CI.
6. **DRAFT PR / CI:** create a bounded branch and Draft PR linked to the Issue;
   provide base/full HEAD, tests, failures, risks and rollback. Run actual native
   CI and record results for that exact HEAD; refresh evidence after changes.
   A docs/Kit check does not substitute for native platform/security gates.
7. **INDEPENDENT REVIEW:** author verification, independent technical review
   (including ChatGPT when requested), formal GitHub approval and owner merge
   authority are separate. Keep Draft until required independent acceptance.
8. **OWNER-AUTHORIZED MERGE:** no standing merge permission. Never merge, deploy,
   publish, change GitHub administration/global settings or access credentials
   without explicit authorization and applicable gates. Do not use RDC or
   RelayForge runtime. Green CI and review do not grant deployment authority.
9. **CLEANUP:** inventory own temporary resources, worktrees, branches, processes,
   dirty/untracked content and open PRs first; check disk use before heavy work
   if low. Remove only obsolete, recoverable, unused own artifacts within scope
   after provenance review. Refuse deletion of user worktrees/branches/data,
   unknown files, unique evidence or open Draft PR work. No forced clean/prune,
   age-based deletion or background cleanup. Preserve uncertain resources.
10. **REPORT:** provide changes, repository/PR links, full HEAD, actual tests,
    exact-head CI, independent-review status, limitations and cleanup inventory.
    Keep source preparation, installation and live operation evidence separate.

Local rules may strengthen gates and specify architecture; they cannot silently
weaken this shared workflow or manufacture owner authorization. Propose exceptions
explicitly in review. Roadmaps and labels are navigation, not another task queue.
contents..github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/task.yml:
name: Task
description: Bounded development task
title: "[Task] "
body:
  - type: textarea
    id: goal
    attributes:
      label: Goal and evidence
      description: Current behavior, desired outcome and supporting evidence.
    validations:
      required: true
  - type: textarea
    id: scope
    attributes:
      label: Scope, non-goals and dependencies
    validations:
      required: true
  - type: textarea
    id: acceptance
    attributes:
      label: Acceptance and native verification
      description: Commands, platforms, security checks and observable success.
    validations:
      required: true
  - type: textarea
    id: risks
    attributes:
      label: Risks, data impact and rollback
  - type: dropdown
    id: priority
    attributes:
      label: Priority
      options:
        - P2 planned
        - P0 critical
        - P1 blocking
        - P3 later
  - type: input
    id: area
    attributes:
      label: Work kind and primary area
      description: Reuse existing labels; this form does not synchronize labels.

contents..project-template/OWNERSHIP.md:
# Ownership and compatibility

| Files / rules | Canonical owner | Consumer treatment |
| --- | --- | --- |
| AGENTS.md, .github/DEVELOPMENT_INTERFACE.md, Task/PR templates, docs/WORKFLOW.md, this map | project-template | Hash-locked managed administration; exact-path review |
| README, docs/INDEX, ARCHITECTURE, TESTING, SECURITY, PROJECT, ADR scaffolds, editorconfig, gitignore | project-template initial scaffold | Consumer-owned after creation; manual reviewed improvements |
| AGENTS.local.md, native CI, product rules and code | Consumer | Never synchronized; stronger gates retained |
| CLI, bundles, locks, sync safety, validators and technical skills | Engineering Kit | Separately pinned Kit channel |
| Kit contract/AGENT_COMMON.md and contract/DEVELOPMENT_INTERFACE.md | Kit legacy v0.1 snapshot | Historical provenance only in new template; not active policy |

Audit: the legacy Kit contracts duplicate lifecycle, review and cleanup policy;
the interface also repeats the agent block and names historical products/native
gates. Preserve bytes for accepted v0.1 consumers and checker compatibility.
Do not extend those copies with new shared lifecycle policy. New consumers use
the template interface exclusively; technical skills remain opt-in references.
Existing consumers migrate in an explicit PR: inventory active references, retain
native gates in AGENTS.local.md, review replacement of old entrypoints, adopt the
administrative lock, then remove legacy policy activation. Never silently replace
an existing AGENTS.md: initial collision must fail. Existing snapshots continue
to work until individually migrated; no global switch or contract rewrite.

Administrative releases use full source commit SHAs in .project-template/lock.json;
Kit uses .engineering-kit/lock.json independently. Scaffold/local docs deliberately
do not receive automatic updates. Propose manual improvements without overwriting
project content. Both distributions remain private pending owner publication review.
contents.AGENTS.md:
# Agent entrypoint

Read [.github/DEVELOPMENT_INTERFACE.md](.github/DEVELOPMENT_INTERFACE.md),
[docs/INDEX.md](docs/INDEX.md), then [AGENTS.local.md](AGENTS.local.md).
The interface is the single shared lifecycle policy. This entrypoint is managed;
put project rules and native commands in AGENTS.local.md, never fork the lifecycle.
User instructions and stronger project constraints prevail; report conflicts and
stop only dependent work. These files grant no additional execution authority.
Engineering Kit contracts bundled under .engineering-kit/contract are frozen
legacy provenance, not a second active administrative policy. Kit skills are
reference material, not implicitly installed or executed.
contents.docs/WORKFLOW.md:
# Workflow

The normative lifecycle lives only in
[the development interface](../.github/DEVELOPMENT_INTERFACE.md).
Use the Task Issue form and PR evidence template; read
[project-native gates](../AGENTS.local.md) before implementation.
For centralized changes use the reviewed [upgrade procedure](UPGRADING.md).
This navigation file is managed; keep local workflow details in PROJECT.md.
